title: Engineer 1:1 scratch - initiative review & growth signals
content:
Context and objective:
- Quick prep for my weekly 1:1 with Elliot (report). Primary goals: unblock project work, calibrate expectations on delivery for the inference-optimizer spike, surface early career signals and make a concrete growth action plan. Keep it under 30 min.

High-level notes/to-self before meeting:
- Elliot shipped the KV cache prototype (branch: kv-cache-experiments). Need to hear perf numbers, latency delta at p95, and memory tradeoffs.
- He mentioned feeling stretched across two initiatives (optimize batching + infra reliability stories) — objective is to help prioritize & set scope.
- Career angle: he asked last week about moving toward tech lead responsibilities; want to map 2‑3 concrete steps he can take in the next 6 weeks.
- Review last 1:1 action items: did he post the perf dashboard screenshots to the sprint channel? (answer: partial) did he create the design doc ticket? (answer: yes, in draft).

Agenda (target 25 minutes)
1) Quick personal check-in (2-3m) - energy, interruptions, any non-work blockers
2) Project health: KV cache prototype + batching opt (8-10m) - data + decisions needed
   - Quick ask: show the perf numbers (p50/p95/p99), memory footprint, cost per-token estimate if we use caching for small-context models.
   - Decision to make: ship prototype to staging behind feature flag this sprint? If yes, owner & rollout steps.
3) Prioritization / scope (5m) - reconcile two initiatives
   - If capacity limited, recommend prioritizing one: lean toward reliability stories if oncall risk is high; otherwise prioritize batching if immediate cost benefit > 12% (benchmark threshold).
4) Career conversation (5-7m) - growth steps and expectations
   - Suggest shadow TL on one rollout, lead a mini design review, write a short postmortem for a past incident.
5) Action items + quick sync cadence check (2m)

Pre-read requests I sent to Elliot: (to check during meeting)
- Link: PR #218 (kv-cache prototype) — ask for top 3 diffs vs baseline
- Tiny dashboard snapshot: latency_by_seq_len.png, mem_profile.png (in #sprint-infra thread)
- Draft design doc: DOC-1147 (staging only)

Key metrics to ask for / validate (quick checklist)
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) before vs after patch (same seq len distribution)
- Memory delta at 80/90/95th percentile traffic
- Estimated cost per 1M tokens change (rough ballpark OK)
- Successful request rate (errors/sec) while running the prototype under small load test

Possible notes / hypotheses to probe
- Hypothesis A: KV cache reduces per-token compute for repeated prefixes by 20-30% on long-dialog workloads; good win for chat products but might add mem pressure — need to validate eviction policy overhead.
- Hypothesis B: Batching optimization yields diminishing returns for low-latency SLO routes—if p95 degrades we should favor cache + smarter routing over larger batches.

Signals of risk / blocking to escalate
- If prototype increases OOM events or adds >2% error-rate in 1k qps test -> pause rollout and triage with SRE.
- If rollout requires infra changes that need infra tickets older than 5 business days to clear -> consider engaging infra PM.

Career/growth checklist (tailored coaching items)
- Lead a mini-design review: prepare a 10-min demo + 2 slide summary. (Outcome: practice public technical communication)
- Pair on on-call runbook improvements: propose 2 concrete edits to runbook and owner for one of them.
- Mentorship: ask him to mentor a junior engineer on writing unit tests for batching module (shared ownership).
- Timeline: pick 1 of the above to complete in ~4 weeks, the rest in ~8-12 weeks.

Draft action items (capture live during 1:1)
- A1: Elliot to post perf dashboard screenshots to #sprint-infra and tag me — due: 2026-03-13 (owner: Elliot)
- A2: If p95 improvement >=12% and mem delta < 10% then feature-flag rollout to staging this sprint — owner: Elliot, with canary plan by 2026-03-19
- A3: Write TLDR for design doc and assign doc owner for final review — due 2026-03-18 (owner: Elliot)
- A4: Elliot to run a 1k qps load test with both patch and baseline and post results — due 2026-03-15 (owner: Elliot + infra help request to SRE if needed)
- A5: Career step: sign up to lead the April mini-design review (owner: Elliot) — due commit by 2026-03-20
- A6: I (Jasmin) to introduce Elliot to Leila for TL shadowing and send calendar invite — due 2026-03-12 (owner: Jasmin)

Notes-to-self for meeting cadence & follow-up
- If he commits to the staging rollout, I’ll schedule a 15-min sync next Friday to check canary metrics.
- If he misses two consecutive deliverable due dates, escalate to direct manager checkpoint and reset scope.

Quick list of conversational prompts (saves time)
- "What surprised you in the perf numbers?"
- "If you had to drop one secondary task, which would it be?"
- "What small win this week made you feel proud?"
- "Which part of the rollout would make you nervous?"

Potential red flags to watch for in the chat:
- Vagueness about test harness setup or inability to point to concrete numbers -> schedule pairing time with infra for reproducibility
- Overcommitment signs: says yes to both initiatives without proposing scope reductions

If time remains (optional):
- Quick check on wellbeing: any PTO planning, mentoring bandwidth, burnout signals?
- Ask for 1-2 retrospective bullets on the previous sprint (what to stop/start/continue)

Post-meeting follow-up template (copy/paste to Slack or email)
- "Thanks — good sync. Recap: A1 (perf screenshots to #sprint-infra by 3/13), A4 (1k qps test by 3/15), A2 (rollout decision by 3/19). I'll intro you to Leila for TL shadowing today. Ping me if anything slips. — Jasmin"

Random scratch/notes (stream-of-consciousness; keep for context)
- Reminder: check on infra ticket aging for the batching infra request (ticket JIRA-OP-882)
- Follow-up: ask Leila for 15m prep tips for leading mini design review
- Consider recommending Elliot try the "one-decision-per-day" experiment when juggling parallel projects

End of doc.
